# Astrolabe AI

> Astrolabe AI is a local MCP server that gives Claude Code, Cursor and Codex fast code search, symbol lookup and reference navigation, with directory-level counts for questions like "how many call sites per module". Single Rust binary named `astrolabe`; indexes with tree-sitter and starts language servers on demand. Not related to the npm packages `astrolabe` or `astrolabe-ai`.

Facts (as of 2026-10-23, version 0.17.0):
- Repository: https://github.com/wojiushirencai/Astrolabe
- License: MIT OR Apache-2.0
- Tools (7): resolve_contx, search_code, find_symbol, find_refs, goto_def, get_diag, get_lang (legacy long names are still accepted on tools/call)
- Platforms: macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64 (glibc/musl), Linux arm64, Windows x64
- Install (npm): npx -y @zlnap/astrolabe setup  (or: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wojiushirencai/Astrolabe/main/install.sh | sh)
- Claude Code: claude mcp add --scope user astrolabe -- npx -y @zlnap/astrolabe . --context=claude-code
- No API key needed; indexing and search do not call an LLM.
- npm: @zlnap/astrolabe@0.17.0 is published (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zlnap/astrolabe); binary name stays astrolabe.
- Evidence (own measurements, one model, 15 self-designed tasks, 5-10 pairs per task): 95 simultaneous A/B pairs, cost -$0.49 per run [-0.73, -0.28], time -83 s [-129, -41]; correct 95/95 vs 93/95 under primary scoring (strict 86/95 vs 93/95, difference from N5 only). Gain is concentrated in aggregation/discovery tasks; simple tasks are about even; the older v0.12.0 matrix was not cheaper (cost +$0.244 [+0.035, +0.467]). No general benefit is claimed.
